DISEASES OF THE GALLBLADDER
Disorders of the biliary tract affect millions of people each year, 
causing significant suffering and even death by precipitating 
pancreatitis and sepsis. A diverse spectrum of disease affects the 
biliary system, often presenting with similar clinical signs and 
symptoms. Treatment may involve diet, medication, or surgery.
Cholestasis
Pathophysiology and Medical Management
Cholestasis is a condition in which little or no bile is secreted 
or the flow of bile into the digestive tract is obstructed. This can 
occur in patients without oral or enteral feeding for a pro-
longed period, such as those requiring PN, and can predispose 
to acalculous cholecystitis. BSEP deficiency results in several 
different genetic forms of cholestasis and acquired forms of 
cholestasis such as drug-induced cholestasis and intrahepatic 
cholestasis of pregnancy (Lam et al, 2010). Prevention of cho-
lestasis requires stimulation of biliary motility and secretions by 
at least minimum enteral feedings. If this is not possible, drug 
therapy is used.
Cholelithiasis
Pathophysiology
